Hi Alex —

Quick answers to your engineering questions: 

1) Embeddings at scale (8M docs)\- Recommended: float16 quantized embeddings with per-batch sizing of ~256-1024 depending on GPU memory. For nightly bulk indexing we typically stream in batches of ~512 and use our batched embedding endpoint which supports async jobs and checkpointing. Memory footprint depends on embedding dim (e.g., 1024 dims at f16 ~ 2KB per vector in memory); plan for ~16–24GB RAM overhead on the worker for 8M vectors during processing.

2) Auth (OIDC -> Redwood)\- We support short-lived token exchange via our token-exchange endpoint: you can exchange an OIDC assertion for a scoped Redwood temporary key (ttl configurable). Implementation options:
  - Server side: exchange assertion on your token service, mint Redwood token for backend jobs
  - CI/CD / dev: we provide a small CLI helper in the quickstart to pull a temporary key using your OIDC client creds

3) Local dev / testing\- Yes — the quickstart can run fully locally: the repo includes a mock-server (node/python) that simulates the Redwood runtime and a Docker compose for local embedding/kv mocks. Env checklist included in the README: Python v3.10+, node 18+, REDWOOD_API_KEY (or local token file), and optional REDWOOD_LOCAL=true for mocks.

Sample snippet (Python) to call the embeddings route locally:

import os
from redwood import RedwoodClient

client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.environ.get('REDWOOD_API_KEY'), base_url=os.environ.get('REDWOOD_BASE_URL'))
emb = client.embeddings.create(model='redwood-embed-1', input=['doc text 1', 'doc text 2'])

For reranking/structured output we include a TypeScript sample that demonstrates function calling to a search microservice and deterministic JSON schema enforcement.

I attached the architecture diagram that maps the routing/wire for SDK integration. Happy to expand any of these with example configs.
